hits.title: Design of a Query Expression for Multi-Dimensional Graph Warehousing
hits.abstract: This study presents an extension of the conventional data warehouse query paradigm by introducing Multi-dimensional Graph eXpression (MGX), a multidimensional query framework designed to support Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) over graph-based business intelligence data. MGX extends the traditional Multi-Dimensional eXpression (MDX) syntax used in relational data warehouses by incorporating SQL-style analytical constructs, including GROUP BY, HAVING, and ORDER BY, thereby improving the expressive capability and flexibility of multidimensional analysis over graph warehouses. By bridging relational data warehousing technologies with graph-based analytical environments, the proposed framework addresses key limitations of traditional MDX in supporting graph-oriented analytics. It enables more effective exploration of semantically rich and socially connected knowledge embedded in networked datasets. Overall, MGX provides a practical methodological foundation for advancing graph warehousing and supporting next-generation network-centric business intelligence applications.

hits.title: Temporal and linguistic enrichment for abstractive text summarization using transformer models
hits.abstract: Abstractive text summarization is a critical yet challenging task in natural language processing, requiring models to generate concise, coherent, and factually accurate summaries. Existing transformer-based architectures, such as BART and T5, often underperform in scenarios where language semantics evolve over time or when lexical diversity is limited. These limitations result in summaries that lack contextual relevance and semantic generalization, especially in dynamic domains such as news reporting. In this work, we present a lightweight hybrid abstractive summarization model that enhances temporal awareness and linguistic flexibility. The model integrates synonym-based augmentation and time-sensitive embeddings into a base transformer encoder-decoder architecture, enabling the generation of temporally aligned and semantically enriched summaries. To further improve reliability, we introduce a factual alignment evaluation module that assesses entity-level consistency using named entity recognition. We conduct extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets, XSum and CNN/Daily Mail, and evaluate the model using a wide range of metrics, including ROUGE, BLEU, METEOR, BERTScore, and factual consistency checks. The ablation study confirms the individual contributions of temporal modeling and synonym enrichment, with the combined model achieving up to 8.3% ROUGE-1 and 7.9% METEOR improvements over the baseline. The model demonstrates practical applicability for summarization systems requiring both temporal relevance and semantic robustness, while maintaining CPU efficiency and interpretability. Implications for downstream tasks like news trend analysis are also explored.

hits.title: Collaborative APT detection through cloud-edge synergy of graph transformer and lightweight clustering
hits.abstract: With the increasing stealth and severity of cyberattacks, the demand for advanced persistent threat (APT) detection systems that deeply understand complex system behaviors has grown substantially. However, existing provenance-based methods often struggle to balance prediction accuracy with inference latency across distributed, resource-constrained environments. To address this, we propose CE-GTC , a collaborative intelligence framework that synergizes large and small models across the cloud-edge continuum. Specifically, the system constructs provenance graphs to capture causal system interactions. In the cloud, a heavy Graph Transformer (the large model) performs computationally intensive representation learning—utilizing edge-feature injection and self-supervised objectives—to extract discriminative embeddings and compact normal behavior profiles. Meanwhile, edge devices host a lightweight clustering detector (the small model) for real-time, privacy-aware anomaly detection via Inverse Document Frequency (IDF)-weighted hybrid distance computation against multi-cluster centers. Experimental evaluations on the Unicorn Wget and StreamSpot datasets demonstrate that CE-GTC achieves superior performance, including an F1-score up to 0.974 and response latency under one second. This highlights the effectiveness of large-small model synergy for scalable, secure, and intelligent APT detection.

hits.title: Intelligent System for Fake User Detection in Social Networks Using Dragon Fly-Neural Network Approach
hits.abstract: In the recent era, social network is a powerful technology to express our views and build the new friendship. But, due to easy process of creating the account in social network, there are number of fake users in the network. Due to the fake users, the fraudulent messages are spread in the network. In this paper, the clustering-based approach is proposed for identifying the fake user in the unattributed static social network. Here, the twitter data set is used to detect the fake users in it. The dataset is represented in graph based on its connections. The nodes in graph are grouped together to form a community using dragon fly clustering. The nodes which are having high Jaccard index are determined as outlier node in the community-based data. Because, this node act as a bridge between the community and it does not belong to any particular community. The optimal feature is detected using Dragon Fly – Neural Network (DF-NN) algorithm by reducing the error rate of the classifier to detect the fake nodes. The proposed method is evaluated using Accuracy and True positive rate with the existing PCA-SVM classification method.

hits.title: A Survey of Link Prediction in Temporal Networks
hits.abstract: Temporal networks have gained significant prominence in the past decade for modelling dynamic interactions within complex systems. A key challenge in this domain is Temporal Link Prediction (TLP), which aims to forecast future connections by analysing historical network structures across a range of applications. While existing surveys have addressed specific aspects of TLP, they typically lack a comprehensive framework that distinguishes between representation and inference methods, the two key ingredients of TLP. This survey bridges this gap by introducing a novel taxonomy that explicitly examines representation and inference in existing methods, providing a novel classification of approaches for TLP. We analyse how different representation techniques capture temporal and structural dynamics, examining their compatibility with various inference methods for link prediction tasks. Our taxonomy not only clarifies the methodological landscape but also reveals promising unexplored combinations of existing techniques. This taxonomy provides a systematic foundation for tackling emerging challenges in TLP, including model explainability and scalable architectures for complex temporal networks.

hits.title: GIL-DDI: multi-view graph invariant learning for unknown drug–drug interaction prediction
hits.abstract: Drug–drug interaction (DDI) prediction is essential for evaluating the side effects of a new drug and adverse interactions before the clinical application. The latest research applies multi-view data to enhance the generalization ability of models to predict new drug interactions, mainly unknown drug–drug interaction (uDDI). However, a new drug’s feature inevitably encounters the feature-shift problem; the trained models have not previously learned information about the new drug, significantly decreasing the uDDI prediction’s accuracy. Thus, we proposed the GIL-DDI model that tries to extract the invariant features of known drugs, alleviating the impact of the feature-shift problem on the prediction of uDDI. In essence, a graph attention network (GAT) initially embeds multi-view knowledge graphs of known drugs, capturing features from chemical entities, substructures, and interactions. Inspired by invariant learning, we subsequently construct a robust feature space of these stable, known-drug characteristics. In the context of a novel pharmaceutical agent, the GAT is employed to initially embed its unique characteristics. Subsequently, these features are fused with the invariant features borrowed from the most similar known drugs in the feature space. This fusion enables the model to enhance the representation of the new drug, thereby addressing issues such as data scarcity and feature-shift problems. Extensive experiments on real-world drug datasets indicate that the proposed method achieves new state-of-the-art records on new drug DDI prediction tasks. The source code is available at https://github.com/davidwushi1145/GIL-DDI .

hits.title: Advanced Analytics and Threat Intelligence
hits.abstract: This chapter presents a comprehensive framework for implementing advanced analytical techniques that transform heterogeneous security data into actionable threat intelligence, addressing critical challenges in modern cybersecurity environments where organizations must process massive volumes of disparate data sources. The content systematically covers the complete threat intelligence lifecycle from planning and data collection through analysis, dissemination, and feedback optimization, exploring core analytical techniques including natural language processing for unstructured security documents, predictive analytics for vulnerability management, time series analysis for security forecasting, graph analysis for mapping attack relationships, and network visualization for threat hunting. Advanced methodologies include automated threat report analysis, social media and dark web intelligence gathering, and threat intelligence platform integration, with each technique presented with practical implementation guidance, performance metrics, and integration considerations for enterprise environments. The chapter emphasizes the paradigm shift from reactive security operations to predictive, intelligence-driven approaches that enable organizations to anticipate and prevent attacks, providing practical case studies, implementation frameworks, and hands-on exercises that equip readers with actionable knowledge for deploying these techniques, while demonstrating how artificial intelligence integration creates transformational capabilities that enable smaller security teams to achieve superior outcomes compared to traditional manual approaches.

hits.title: Temporal Graph Classification Based on Fast and Exact Transitive Reduction Strategy
hits.abstract: Temporal graphs are a variety of structured data that have been particularly studied recently. In this paper, we focus on classification of temporal graphs. Previous works have shown that such task can be tackled by first transforming temporal graphs to static ones using ad-hoc algorithms, before the classification step. However, resulting static graphs might be of huge size. Transitive reduction can be used to reduce the size and redundancy of such graphs, but with a high complexity time. In this paper, we propose a fully dynamic algorithm that transforms temporal graphs into static ones while applying exact transitive reduction at the same time. This algorithm has a much reduced complexity than doing both steps separately, while producing exactly the same output graphs. We show in the experimental section that similar accuracy is achieved for a lower computational time.

hits.title: Part-GNN: A Partitioning-Based Graph Neural Network for Efficient Memory Large Scale Data Classification
hits.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are a class of deep learning models that have demonstrated significant potential in various classification tasks, including image recognition and the prediction of labels for nodes and edges. Unlike traditional neural networks that operate on Euclidean data such as images or sequences, GNNs are specifically designed to handle non-Euclidean data, i.e. data represented as graphs, where relationships between entities are irregular and complex. These graphs may include rich node and edge attributes, making GNNs particularly suitable for domains such as social networks, molecular structures, and recommendation systems. Several GNN variants have been developed, including GCN, Cluster-GCN, GraphSAGE, and FastGCN. Despite their advantages, GNNs often require substantial memory, primarily due to the large adjacency matrices involved, which become computationally expensive for large-scale graphs. They also tend to have long training times. In this work, we propose a novel graph partitioning technique aimed at reducing the effective size of the graph while maintaining a high predictive F1-score. Furthermore, we integrate this partitioning approach with layer-wise training to enhance computational efficiency.

hits.title: Enhancing 3D shape recognition with multi-view relational transformer networks
hits.abstract: 3D shape recognition is pivotal in computer vision, with applications spanning autonomous driving, digital twins, and cultural heritage preservation. This paper introduces MVRT-Net, a novel Multi-View Relational Transformer Network, addressing the challenge of balancing local details and global context in 3D shape descriptors. MVRT-Net integrates a Multi-Scale Adaptive Dynamic Graph Attention mechanism and a Transformer-based global view relational modeling strategy with adaptive key-view selection and adaptive attention pooling, which dynamically learns view-level importance weights to suppress redundant information and fuse cross-scale semantics into a more discriminative global descriptor. Experimental results on the ModelNet40 dataset demonstrate MVRT-Net’s superiority, achieving a classification accuracy of 97.89%, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Our approach sets a new benchmark in 3D shape recognition by offering a favorable accuracy–complexity trade-off and robust feature representation. Our project repository is available at: https://github.com/weihai0226/MVRT/tree/master/MVRT .

hits.title: IGNC: multimodal fake news detection based on interactive graphic network compression
hits.abstract: With the rapid development of social media, the generation and dissemination of fake news have become increasingly convenient, making fake news detection a widespread challenge in the field of information dissemination. Existing non-graph-based deep learning methods often struggle to effectively model complex relationships across multimodal data. In contrast, Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) can model multimodal data as graph structures to better capture intricate intermodal relationships, though incurring substantial computational overhead. To address these challenges, we propose the Interactive Graph Network Compression (IGNC) model. This model employs a fine-grained graph construction module to extract rich unimodal feature representations and construct unimodal graph structures. It then utilizes a semantic-based graph compression module to eliminate semantically redundant connections. Finally, through a multimodal graph interaction module, it achieves a stable transformation from unimodal to multimodal graph structures. By enhancing intra-modal and inter-modal information interaction through attention mechanisms, the model learns more robust news representations. Experiments on public datasets demonstrate that IGNC significantly improves fake news detection accuracy while effectively reducing semantic redundancy.

raw_metadata.title: Temporal and linguistic enrichment for abstractive text summarization using transformer models
raw_metadata.abstract: Abstractive text summarization is a critical yet challenging task in natural language processing, requiring models to generate concise, coherent, and factually accurate summaries. Existing transformer-based architectures, such as BART and T5, often underperform in scenarios where language semantics evolve over time or when lexical diversity is limited. These limitations result in summaries that lack contextual relevance and semantic generalization, especially in dynamic domains such as news reporting. In this work, we present a lightweight hybrid abstractive summarization model that enhances temporal awareness and linguistic flexibility. The model integrates synonym-based augmentation and time-sensitive embeddings into a base transformer encoder-decoder architecture, enabling the generation of temporally aligned and semantically enriched summaries. To further improve reliability, we introduce a factual alignment evaluation module that assesses entity-level consistency using named entity recognition. We conduct extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets, XSum and CNN/Daily Mail, and evaluate the model using a wide range of metrics, including ROUGE, BLEU, METEOR, BERTScore, and factual consistency checks. The ablation study confirms the individual contributions of temporal modeling and synonym enrichment, with the combined model achieving up to 8.3% ROUGE-1 and 7.9% METEOR improvements over the baseline. The model demonstrates practical applicability for summarization systems requiring both temporal relevance and semantic robustness, while maintaining CPU efficiency and interpretability. Implications for downstream tasks like news trend analysis are also explored.

hits.title: A line graph-based metric learning framework for robust link prediction in complex networks
hits.abstract: Link prediction is a fundamental task in network analysis, yet existing methods face two key limitations: they capture edge relationships only indirectly through node-level comparisons and are sensitive to the severe class imbalance inherent in sparse graphs. Reformulating link prediction as node classification on line graphs addresses both issues by elevating edges to first-class entities, thereby enabling direct relationship modeling. This transformation, however, can lead to quadratic growth in the number of nodes and edges, rendering naive implementations computationally infeasible at scale. To address this challenge, we propose LineML , a scalable line graph framework built on three complementary components: (i) a GraphSAGE-based architecture for multi-hop structural aggregation, (ii) an adaptive metric learning module with degree-biased negative sampling to mitigate class imbalance, and (iii) a spectral pruning strategy combined with multi-GPU training to manage computational complexity. Evaluated on 18 benchmark datasets against 14 state-of-the-art baselines, LineML achieves the best average rank on social and biological networks with strong statistical dominance (Cliff’s $$\delta \ge 0.97$$ δ ≥ 0.97 , $$p < 0.01$$ p < 0.01 ), along with substantial improvements on citation networks. These gains are accompanied by up to a $$4.6\times$$ 4.6 × reduction in training time on a single GPU and up to a $$14\times$$ 14 × speedup on a dual-GPU system.

hits.title: Adaptive competitive balance regulation in professional sports leagues via graph attention networks and proximal policy optimization
hits.abstract: Sustaining competitive balance underpins both the commercial vitality and fan engagement of professional sports leagues, yet most regulatory regimes still rely on static rules that cannot track shifting competitive dynamics. We present an integrated framework that couples graph attention networks (GATs) with proximal policy optimization (PPO) for adaptive, data-driven regulatory policy design. The league is cast as a weighted directed graph in which clubs are nodes and edges encode match outcomes, financial flows, and dominance relations. A multi-layer GAT encoder distills this graph into a compact state vector that retains relational patterns across structural scales, and a PPO agent acts on that vector to optimize multi-instrument regulatory actions—salary caps, revenue-sharing ratios, and draft lottery parameters—over multi-season horizons. A composite reward balances competitive parity, revenue preservation, and policy stability. In simulation experiments calibrated to twenty seasons of English Premier League (EPL) and National Basketball Association (NBA) data, the proposed GAT-PPO framework attains competitive balance improvement rates of 32.7% (95% CI: [30.3%, 35.1%]) and 22.1% (95% CI: [19.9%, 24.3%]), respectively, outperforming fixed-rule baselines and ablated variants at statistically significant levels (paired t-test, p < 0.01, Bonferroni-corrected). To remove any ambiguity about comparability, every baseline is evaluated under the same simulator, the same observation frequency, the same state-space dimensionality, and the same five random seeds; this fairness protocol is detailed in Sect. 4.1. Interpretability analysis shows context-sensitive regulatory behavior: interventions intensify under severe imbalance and relax once parity overshoots the target. All results derive from a calibrated simulation environment with bounded-rational agent assumptions. We do not treat “simulation-based” as the endpoint of validation. Instead, we propose and partially execute a three-stage real-world validation pathway: (i) distributional face-validity checks against twenty seasons of historical EPL and NBA data using Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests on RSD, HHI, and Gini indices; (ii) directional concordance backtesting against four documented regulatory interventions (NBA 2011 CBA reform, EPL 2013 FFP introduction, NBA 2017 apron rule, EPL 2018 PSR tightening); and (iii) zero-shot transfer to a third league (MLB) outside the training distribution. Together these findings demonstrate the practical promise of pairing graph-structured deep learning with sequential decision-making for league governance.

hits.title: Valorization of Low Quality Dates for Syrup Production: Effect of Processing Conditions on Chemical Functional Properties
hits.abstract: Over the past few decades, there has been a substantial rise in date production in Tunisia. However, this growth in production has been marred by a notable increase in losses incurred during harvesting, storage, marketing, and technological processing. The significant quantities of by-products resulting from these losses remain largely unused by the population due to their poor quality. Biotechnological processing of lower-quality dates with a hard texture into derived products may give them a presentation, a structure and functionality. The aim of this work is to enhance the value of date fruit of inferior grades by using it in syrup production made according to different processing conditions. Four processes for date syrup preparation were used: conventional, by enzymatic extraction, microwave and intermittent processes (conventional—microwave) were investigated. The corresponding syrups were characterized and compared. The overall phenolic (TPC) and flavonoid (TFC) concentrations, along with their associated antioxidant capabilities were performed for each sample of the date syrup. Results showed effective outcomes of the used process for date syrup preparation on their functional properties. Date syrup prepared according to the combined process gave the highest phenolic and flavonoid contents (504.127 mg Gallic Acid Equivalent/100 g and 190.892 mg Catechin Equivalent/100 g of syrup respectively). The results of our study hold significant relevance for both researchers in the field and the fruit-processing industry. They offer opportunities to create novel food products with elevated antioxidant properties, aligning with the preferences of a contemporary consumer demographic.

hits.title: Tunisian Acorn (Quercus ilex): An Alternative Source of Flour in Cereal and Gluten-Free Products
hits.abstract: In the Mediterranean region, acorn fruits were generally used as animal feed for thousand years. At present, acorns are traditionally used for human consumption especially in bread and cake recipes. Thus, the objective of the present work was to highlight the interest of valorizing acorn fruits ( Quercus ilex ) from the north of Tunisia for the preparation of acorn flour as an alternative source of common wheat flour in order to produce cereal and gluten-free products. In this regard, the biochemical composition of the obtained acorn flour was studied. The phytochemical analysis in term of total contents of phenolics (TPC), tannins (TCT), flavonoids (TFC), and the HPLC profiles of the phenolic acids present in acorn flour extract were also determined as well as the composition of extracted acorn oil using gas chromatography. After that, the extracted acorn flour was mixed with semolina, wheat flour, and other gluten-free flours to determine the effect of its incorporation during the preparation of bread, pasta, muffin, cookies, and pizza. Results showed that acorn flour moisture was about 14.2%, whereas protein, ash, fat, and carbohydrates contents were 8.5%, 1.02%, 8.5%, and 66.78%, respectively. For TPC, TFC, and TCT, their contents in acorn flour were respectively, 20.55 mg GAE/g DW, 9.05 mg CE/g DW, and 1.21 mg GAE/g DW. In addition, we noted that the main phenolic acids were protocatechuic acid, ferulic acid, and gallic acid. Besides, oleic, linoleic, and palmitic were shown to be the main identified fatty acids in acorn fruits oil. Then, the efficiency of the substitution of wheat flour by the extracted acorn flour alone or in combination with other gluten-free flours was evaluated by pilot productions of cereal product such as: bread, pasta, muffin, cookies, and pizza. Results showed that the nutritional and rheological qualities of the formulated cereal products were improved with acceptable sensory properties.

hits.title: The Potential Impact of Agrivoltaic in Food Production: The Case Study of Chicory Crop
hits.abstract: The international policies promoting renewable energy to reduce greenhouse gas emissions have resulted in agricultural land being converted to photovoltaic installations, leading to losses in food production. Agrivoltaics are systems that combine agricultural practices with solar energy production. Such systems involve installing photovoltaic (PV) panels on agricultural land or integrating them into structures such as greenhouses or shade structures. The primary goal of agrivoltaic systems is to maximize land use multifunctionality by promoting simultaneously solar energy for electricity production and carrying out agricultural activities. However, the agrivoltaic systems need careful planning and design to ensure that the shadow generated by PV panels doesn’t negatively impact crop production. Different crops have varying light requirements, and the orientation and height of the PV panels should be optimized accordingly. As the development of agrivoltaic farms is relatively new there is little knowledge of its crop production effects; therefore, further experimental applications are needed to assess the shadow and microclimate impacts generated by PV panel’s presence on the crops taking into account the heterogeneity of the agricultural sector. This study analyzed the effects of agricultural production under the shadow plots, mimicking the shadow impact of the PV panels, and in full sun plots as a control area. We chose chicory crop to highlight the differences in quantity and quality of crop production. Management cultivation practices, water availability, and soil composition were equally applied for all the analyzed plots to exclude environmental effects non-linked to the shadow. For each plant, weight, foliage dimension, and total secondary metabolites concentration were measured. The results showed a significantly high capacity of the shading system to increase edible chicory biomass production than the control plot with an increase in average weight biomass of 69%. Moreover, there was no relevant difference in the quality of crop production considering total secondary metabolites concentrations. We cannot exclude that in an agrivoltaic field these differences could be less significant, but it is possible to consider that a well-designed agrivoltaic system could be a good strategy to combine renewable energy strategies with food security increasing agricultural economic income.

hits.title: Legume Flours as an Alternative for Sustainable Consumption
hits.abstract: Recently, there has been a growing interest in exploring novel applications of legume flours as primary ingredients in many recipes by virtue of their dietary richness and notable functional attributes. This study focuses on investigating the physicochemical and functional characteristics of various Tunisian legume flour varieties, including chickpea, fava bean, and lentils, with the aim of proposing them as alternative flours for sustainable dietary practices. The research involved a thorough examination of the physicochemical and techno-functional attributes of these legume flours. The proximate composition analysis revealed that fava bean flour boasts the highest protein content (32.18%) compared to chickpea and lentil flours. Furthermore, in terms of physical attributes, fava bean flour demonstrated the highest Water Solubility Index (24.62%) among the three. Regarding functional properties such as water and Oil Absorption Capacities, Emulsifying and Foaming Capacities, lentil flour exhibited the most significant Foaming Capacity (45%), closely followed by fava bean flour. Additionally, lentil flour showcased the highest Water Absorption Capacity (WAC) at 2.007 g/g, while fava bean flour displayed commendable Oil Absorption Capacity (OAC) at 1.38 g/g, coupled with the lowest Minimal Gelation Concentration (MGC) at 8%. On the other hand, chickpea flour demonstrated superior emulsifying activity and stability (74.17% and 88.33%, respectively) and exhibited the highest antioxidant activity (89.08%) compared to lentils and fava bean flours. In conclusion, this research underscores the high nutritional quality and the potential utilization of legumes in the production of healthy products, particularly as ingredients or functional additives.

hits.title: EEG-Based Confusion Detection Using Conv1D-BiLSTM Model with Multi-head Attention and Entropy-Driven Feature Fusion
hits.abstract: Accurate detection of learner confusion is a critical challenge in adaptive e-learning systems since it may allow for timely feedback and personalized support. In fact, electroencephalogram signals carry the information related to cognitive states directly and reliably; however, their highly variable and non-stationary nature makes classification difficult. Handcrafted statistical or frequency-domain feature-based traditional methods often fail to capture full complexity in EEG dynamics, whereas purely deep learning models might miss complementary handcrafted information. This paper proposes a hybrid deep learning framework that combines raw EEG band sequences with entropy-based descriptors and probabilistic scores generated by a Random Forest classifier. The combined feature set feeds into a neural architecture composed of convolutional, bidirectional LSTM, and attention layers that allow for the effective modeling of both local and long-range temporal dependencies. Experimental results using stratified five-fold cross-validation confirm the robustness of this approach. Our model achieved the best classification accuracy with a value of 95.9% , outperforming state-of-the-art configurations and thus proving to have very strong potential for real-world confusion detection in e-learning environments.

hits.title: Evaluation of the Anti-inflammatory Activity of Artemisia annua Grown in Algeria
hits.abstract: Since immemorial, great civilizations have used medicinal plants for their therapeutic, cosmetic, chemical, dietary, pharmaceutical, food, and industrial properties. Artemisia annua is one of the plants widely used in traditional medicine to combat a variety of pathologies such as malaria, intestinal disorders, and bacterial and viral infections; some countries have even adopted it as a cure for COVID-19. These properties have prompted researchers to evaluate the biological activities of this plant, mainly since it is grown in Algeria. This study explored the potential anti-inflammatory effects of locally grown annual mugwort. To assess the anti-inflammatory potential of a methanolic extract from Artemisia annua L., we utilized the protein denaturation method as outlined in Alhakmani et al. (Asian Pac J Trop Biomed 3(8):623–627, 2013 ). The reaction mixture of the species studied was prepared at different concentrations, and the results were compared with those of acetylsalicylic acid as a standard, which belongs to the group of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). The results showed that mugwort had an inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 0.193 mg/ml lower than that of acetylsalicylic acid at 0.302 mg/ml. This activity comes down to the presence of bioactive molecules that enter signaling. This significant anti-inflammatory activity is linked to the rich flavonoid content of Artemisia annua L. extract and the diversity of phenolic compound types. Our results corroborate with studies evaluating the anti-inflammatory activity of wormwood in other countries. A meaningful relationship is between oxidative stress, inflammation, and pathologies. The biological anti-inflammatory activity suggests that annual mugwort can have more therapeutic potential for treating or preventing certain pathologies.

hits.title: A Novel Hybrid Transformer-Based Framework for Reconstruction-Based ECG Anomaly Detection
hits.abstract: Early detection of heart disorders relies heavily on identifying abnormalities in electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, yet most deep learning methods depend on large annotated datasets, which are difficult to obtain in practice. We present a combined unsupervised framework that leverages the advantages of both Transformers and LSTMs for reconstruction-based anomaly detection. The model is trained only on normal ECG recordings, enabling it to learn the underlying rhythm of healthy cardiac activity. At inference, irregular beats stand out through higher reconstruction errors, separated by a simple threshold. On benchmark datasets, the framework shows strong generalization – achieving 96.67% accuracy on ECG5000 and 96.44% accuracy on MIT-BIH. In our design, we have a lead-specific strategy for PTB-XL where separate models are trained per lead to maintain the small morphological differences, rather than averaging signals. Overall, our proposed method provides accurate, interpretable, and scalable ECG anomaly detection alternatives that we hope will provide a valuable tool for automated monitoring and early screening of arrhythmias.

On benchmark datasets, the framework shows strong generalization – achieving 96.67% accuracy on ECG5000 and 96.44% accuracy on MIT-BIH. In our design, we have a lead-specific strategy for PTB-XL where separate models are trained per lead to maintain the small morphological differences, rather than averaging signals. Overall, our proposed method provides accurate, interpretable, and scalable ECG anomaly detection alternatives that we hope will provide a valuable tool for automated monitoring and early screening of arrhythmias.

hits.title: Real-Time Indian Sign Language Recognition Using Hierarchical Windowed Graph Attention Networks with Motion-Gated Inference and Multi-language Support
hits.abstract: Purpose: Over 5M+ people in India rely on Indian Sign Language for communication with specially-abled people, and yet technological support remains very limited. We developed a real-time ISL recognition system as a proof-of-concept demonstrating CPU-based deployment feasibility. Methods: We adapted and optimized existing HWGAT architecture with 9.7M parameters (52.7% reduction from baseline) processing 29 MediaPipe-extracted keypoints enhanced with Fourier features, cyclic shifts, and learnable positional encodings. Our heuristic motion-gated mechanism uses simple displacement thresholds for continuous sign detection. Results: On a limited 6-class dataset (76 samples), the system achieved 78.57% validation accuracy. The 95% CI (49.2%-95.3%) reflects higher variance due to a small sample size, which indicates that the results should be interpreted as preliminary. Ablation studies show that incremental improvements are as such: learnable encodings (+8.33%), Fourier features (+7.14%), and cyclic shifts (+7.14%). Conclusion: Our work demonstrates the feasibility of a CPU-based ISL recognition but acknowledges its significant limitations: a small vocabulary, limited amount of training data and simpler motion-gating heuristics. Findings established baseline for future large-scale studies.
